questions.title: How many tosses
questions.prompt: A fair coin is tossed $n$ times. Find the least $n$ such that the probability of at least one head exceeds $0.99$.
hints: At least one head is the complement of no heads.
n must be a whole number.

traps.why: With 6 tosses the probability is only 63/64 ≈ 0.984.

questions.title: Is the game fair
questions.prompt: It costs \$5 to roll a fair die. The player wins \$12 for a six, \$3 for a four or five, and nothing otherwise. Find the expected gain per game and comment on whether the game is fair.
hints: A fair game has expected gain 0.

traps.why: Forgot to subtract the 5 dollar cost to play.

questions.label: (i)
questions.title: Two chosen numbers
questions.prompt:
Two people each choose a whole number from $1$ to $5$ independently and at random.

Find the probability that they choose different numbers.
hints: Count the pairs with equal numbers.

traps.why: Gave the probability that the numbers are the same.

questions.label: (ii)
questions.title: Two chosen numbers
questions.prompt:
Two people each choose a whole number from $1$ to $5$ independently and at random.

Find the probability that the product of their numbers is even.

steps.d: The product is odd only if both are odd: $\left(\tfrac35\right)^{2} = \tfrac{9}{25}$.

traps.why: Found P(both even) instead of P(at least one even).

questions.title: Finding the faulty fuses
questions.prompt: A box has $3$ good fuses and $2$ faulty fuses. Fuses are tested one at a time, in random order, until both faulty fuses have been found. Find the probability that exactly three tests are needed.
hints: Think about where the two faulty fuses sit in the order.
Exactly three tests means the second faulty fuse is third.

steps.d: All $\binom52 = 10$ placements of the 2 faulty fuses are equally likely.
Third test is the second faulty one: faulty fuses in positions $\{1,3\}$ or $\{2,3\}$.

traps.why: Counted {1, 2} as finishing at the third test.

questions.label: (ii)
questions.title: Three archers
questions.prompt:
Three archers fire independently at a target. Their probabilities of hitting are $0.7$, $0.6$ and $0.5$.

Find the probability that exactly one archer hits.
hints: In each case the other two miss.

traps.why: Considered only the first archer hitting.

questions.title: Dice summing to eight
questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum is $8$.

traps.why: Counted (4, 4) twice or missed an ordered pair.

questions.title: One of each colour
questions.prompt: A bag has $4$ red and $6$ blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that they are different colours.

questions.title: Expected net gain
questions.prompt: A game costs $\$2$ to play. A fair die is rolled and the player receives $\$6$ if it shows a six, otherwise nothing. Find the expected net gain per game.
hints: Multiply each payout by its probability.

questions.title: Variance of a small distribution
questions.prompt: $X$ takes values $0,1,2$ with probabilities $0.2,0.5,0.3$. Find $\operatorname{Var}(X)$.

questions.title: At least one head
questions.prompt: A fair coin is tossed $4$ times. Find the probability of at least one head.

traps.why: That is P(first toss is a head).

questions.title: Heart or king
questions.prompt: A card is drawn from a standard pack of $52$. Find the probability that it is a heart or a king.

traps.why: Counted the king of hearts twice.

questions.title: Even product of two dice
questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the product of the numbers is even.
hints: Each die is odd with probability ½.

traps.why: Even products are more likely than odd ones.

questions.title: Three aces in a row
questions.prompt: Three cards are drawn without replacement from a standard pack. Find the probability that all three are aces.
hints: Reduce numerator and denominator each time.

questions.title: No six in three rolls
questions.prompt: A fair die is rolled three times. Find the probability that no six appears.
hints: Each roll avoids six with probability 5/6.

questions.title: Recovering an independent probability
questions.prompt: $A$ and $B$ are independent, $P(A)=0.3$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.58$. Find $P(B)$.

questions.title: Choose a box then a ball
questions.prompt: Box $1$ has $3$ white and $2$ black balls; box $2$ has $1$ white and $4$ black. A box is chosen at random and a ball drawn. Find the probability that it is white.

questions.title: Largest number is a six
questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the larger number shown is $6$.

questions.title: Two heads in three tosses
questions.prompt: Three fair coins are tossed. Find the probability of exactly two heads.

questions.title: Variance with a negative value
questions.prompt: $X$ takes values $-1,0,2$ with probabilities $0.3,0.5,0.2$. Find $\operatorname{Var}(X)$.

questions.title: An even sum of two numbers
questions.prompt: Two different numbers are chosen at random from $1,2,3,4,5$. Find the probability that their sum is even.
hints: An even sum needs the same parity.
Count pairs from 3 odds and 2 evens.

steps.d: Both odd: $3$ pairs; both even: $1$ pair

traps.why: Odd and even numbers are not equally many.

questions.title: Expected sixes
questions.prompt: A fair die is rolled $30$ times. Find the expected number of sixes.
hints: Multiply by the number of rolls.
